latin.613: AD POSTERIUS pergit respondere Autor n. 3. p. 329. integra, sequentibus: Nec quicquam jam bis officit, quod à Psychicis quidem omnibus, Barjesuitis, Jesuitisque; (Una enim copulantur, per hanc Sacramenti cauponandi caudam, vulpeculæ istæ;) pro maxima & ineluctabili difficultate jactitatur.
latin.614: Qui, licèt inficias ire nequeant, vel maximè re esse id, quod Spiritualiter est, Quia tamen Suppositum ipsum in sacramento, Res Materialis atque Naturalis est, (corpus putà Christi, in cruce fractum, & sanguis Christi, in cruce fusus;) contendunt ergò, Rei Naturalis nullam veram participationem esse, nisi Naturali aliquo modo; Spiritualiter igitur si solùm à nobis participetur corpus Christi, Verè, atque reipsà non participari.
latin.615: Atque hæc jam illa pugna est, quam clamitant, è cujus sibi per somnium fictione, verè sese protrudunt in Elenchum illum Apostoli (ad neminem unquam magis, quam ad ipsos nunc pertinentem,) etoi eisin hoi apodiorizontes, psychikoi, pneuma mē echontes, Judæ vers. 19. Spiritualem enim omnem corporis Dominici præsentiam cùm ipsi execrentur, & materiæ soli miserè immersi, ultra sensum nihil sapiant, nullamque nisi naturalem, atque psychikēn rationem in sacramento sectentur, fortiter sese jam apodiorizontas præstant, sive illud de Rebus interpretandum sit, Potiorem enim Sacramenti rationem, & quæ Spiritualis veréque Divina est, prorsus exulare jubent; sive de Personis, & tum vel semetipsos excludunt (& à Latino quidem Vulgari, Nostrisque sic redditur:) Ethnicorum planè more, non plùs credentes, quàm ex naturali lumine, seu potiùs crepusculo, assequi possunt; vel saltem, posse se Nos exterminare à Participio Divino sperant.
latin.616: Quia Nos (sed ab ipso Christo edocti, spiritum esse, qui vivificat, carnemque prodesse nihil, Jo. 6. 63.) etiam & verba, quæ hac in re prolata sunt, Spiritum esse & Vitam, Ipsi monenti credimus, proque conditione ipsâ Doctrinæ S. Spiritus, decernimus, spiritualiter ista discernenda esse, & Spiritualia cum Spiritualibus semper conferenda esse, 1. Cor. 2, 13.
latin.617: Addit Auctor subtilissimus Num. 4. p. 330. Corpus Domini in se spectatum, non unô modô exstitisse: Non psychikōs solùm, sed & pneumatikōs etiam: Factus est enim novissimus Adam (h.e. Christus) in spiritum vivificantem 1. Cor. 15. 45. Ecquid impedit, quin, ut existit in se, ita & participetur à nobis? SPIRITUALITER procul omni dubio participari potest; Atque ita satis constabit nobis participatio nostra, sed & verissima ea & principalissima erit. Naturaliter verò ne participari jam possit præfertim per manducationem & bibitionem; Quarum conditio (si humanam naturam pro Objecto suo, habeat) ab ipsâ Naturâ longissimè abhorret. Novimus alios plures obices poni, quibus recensendis nunc non moramur, amovendis quidem ne ipsa Roma sufficit.
latin.618: Quin Num. 5tô. Duplicem hunc existendi Corporis Christi Modum, non minùs ante, quàm post resurrectionem, isti competiisse, evincit ex 1. Cor. 15. De Spirituali existendi modo, ab ipsâ inde corporis Christi conceptione, ita pronuncians: Non ex aliqua virtute Resurrectionis Christus, sed inde à principio, per vim hypostaticæ suæ Unionis, Spiritualitatem corporis ipsam, secum attulisse in uterum B. Virginis. Aliter enim si fuisset, incongruè satis saltem minùs appositè, ab Apostolo, citationem illam præmittente Gen. 2, 7. factus est primus Homo Adam in animam viventem, subjungitur & hoc (quasi quod priùs jam dicto sic respondeat, ut & citi quoque, nonnullis videatur) Factus est novissimus Adam in spiritum vivificantem 1. Cor 15, 45. Primus autem Adam, ab ipso primordio condituræ suæ, in animam viventem factus est. Quæ igitur jam paritas, quæ symphōnēsis aut Correspondentia erit, nisi & secundus Adam in spiritum vivificantem, ab ipso quoque conceptionis suæ momento, ita factus fuerit? p. 331. circa finem.

pass_a.613: To the LATTER the Author continues to reply in n. 3 p. 329 entire, with the following: Nor does anything now twice stand in the way — that which by all the Psychics indeed, the Barjesuits, and the Jesuits as well (for those little foxes are coupled together by this tail of huckstering the Sacrament) is tossed about as the greatest and inescapable difficulty.
pass_a.614: Who, though they cannot deny that even most of all that which is Spiritually is in the thing itself, yet because the Supposit itself in the sacrament is a Material and Natural Thing (namely Christ’s body broken on the cross, and Christ’s blood poured on the cross), they contend therefore that there is no true participation of a Natural Thing except in some Natural mode; if therefore Christ’s body is participated by us only Spiritually, it is not participated Truly and in the thing itself.
pass_a.615: And this now is that fight which they shout — from whose dream-fiction they truly thrust themselves into that Elenchus of the Apostle (now pertaining to no one ever more than to themselves): ‘these are they who separate themselves, psychikoi, not having the spirit,’ Jude v. 19. For when they themselves execrate every Spiritual presence of the Lord’s body, and miserably immersed in matter alone taste nothing beyond sense, and chase no ratio in the sacrament except the natural and psychic one, they strongly show themselves already as those who separate — whether that be interpreted of Things (for they order the better ratio of the Sacrament, which is Spiritual and truly Divine, to be wholly banished) or of Persons (and then they either exclude themselves — and so the Latin Vulgar and ours render it — plainly after the manner of the Gentiles, believing no more than they can attain from natural light, or rather twilight; or at least they hope they can drive Us from Divine Participation).
pass_a.616: Because We (but taught by Christ Himself that it is the spirit that vivifies, and the flesh profits nothing, Jn 6:63) also believe Him when He warns that the words spoken in this matter are Spirit and Life, and according to the very condition of the Holy Spirit’s Doctrine we decide that these things are to be discerned spiritually, and that Spiritual things are always to be compared with Spiritual, 1 Cor. 2:13.
pass_a.617: The most subtle Author adds in Num. 4 p. 330: The Lord’s Body viewed in itself has not existed in one mode only: not psychikōs only, but also pneumatikōs: for the last Adam (i.e. Christ) was made into a life-giving spirit, 1 Cor. 15:45. What hinders that, as it exists in itself, so also it be participated by us? SPIRITUALLY it can without all doubt be participated; and so our participation will stand firm enough for us — nay it will be the truest and most principal. But whether it can now be participated Naturally, especially by eating and drinking — whose condition (if it has human nature for its Object) abhors farthest from Nature itself — we know many other obstacles are set, which we do not now delay to list; for removing them not even Rome itself suffices.
pass_a.618: Nay in Num. 5 he proves from 1 Cor. 15 that this double Mode of Christ’s Body existing belonged to it no less before than after the resurrection. On the Spiritual mode of existing from the very conception of Christ’s body he pronounces thus: Not from some virtue of the Resurrection did Christ, but from the beginning, by the force of His hypostatic Union, bring the body’s own Spirituality with Him into the Blessed Virgin’s womb. For if it had been otherwise, the Apostle would incongruously — or at least less aptly — after prefacing that citation of Gen. 2:7 ‘the first man Adam was made into a living soul’ subjoin also this (as if answering what was already said, so that to some it even seems cited): ‘The last Adam was made into a life-giving spirit,’ 1 Cor. 15:45. But the first Adam from the very beginning of his creation was made into a living soul. What parity then, what symphony or Correspondence, will there be, unless the second Adam also was made into a life-giving spirit from the very moment of His conception? p. 331 near the end.

613: Wren’s AD POSTERIUS (n. 3 p. 329): nothing now blocks twice — the Psychics, Barjesuits, and Jesuits (foxes tied by the same sacrament-huckstering tail) toss this as their greatest inescapable difficulty.
What follows is their material-supposit objection against spiritual participation.
614: They concede that what is spiritual most of all is in the thing itself — yet the sacrament’s supposit is a material natural thing: Christ’s body broken and blood poured on the cross.
So they urge: a natural thing has no true participation except in some natural mode; if Christ’s body is received only spiritually, it is not received truly / in the thing itself.
615: Wren turns their dream-fight into Jude 19’s elenchus: they are the separators — psychikoi without the spirit — now more than anyone.

Immersed in matter alone, they execrate every spiritual presence of the Lord’s body, chase only a natural/psychic sacrament-ratio, and either banish the spiritual-divine ratio of the sacrament or exclude themselves (and hope to drive us) from divine participation — Gentile-style, believing only natural twilight.
616: We follow Christ’s own teaching (Jn 6:63): the spirit vivifies; the flesh profits nothing — and His warning that the words spoken here are Spirit and Life.
Under the Holy Spirit’s doctrine we discern these things spiritually and always set spiritual things with spiritual (1 Cor. 2:13).
617: Wren (n. 4 p. 330): the Lord’s body in itself existed not in one mode only — not psychically alone but also pneumatically. The last Adam (Christ) was made a life-giving spirit (1 Cor. 15:45).

As it exists in itself, so it can be participated: SPIRITUALLY without doubt — our truest and chief participation. Natural eating and drinking of human nature as object abhors farthest from nature; other obstacles Rome itself cannot remove.
618: §.XXIII close (n. 5): the body’s double mode of existing belonged before the resurrection no less than after — spirituality of the body brought from the beginning by hypostatic union into the Virgin’s womb, not first from resurrection power (1 Cor. 15 with Gen. 2:7).
Else Adam’s living-soul / last-Adam life-giving-spirit correspondence fails unless the second Adam was so from conception’s moment. Stop before §.XXIV.
